title: Coupled resources
heading: Coupled resources
text: Coupled resources Coupled resources run in the existing physical-graph labeling framework. Installselected/binary value domains, simultaneous pickup/delivery, cumulative costs,bounded affine or piecewise-linear dependencies, base-state maps, andstate-dependent costs, and free-entry interval-cost fronts with Graph::set_coupled_resources,Solver::set_coupled_resources, or Python ResourceModel.install.No graph expansion or separate pricing front is used by this path.Paired pickup-before-delivery constraints are outside the requested scope.

title: Coupled resources
heading: Resource definitions
text:
Resource definitions All per-arc vectors use the original graph's arc vector order, includingarcs into the sink. They do not use physical arc IDs as array indices.Multiple resources compose in declaration order. Resource Transition Charging Retain continuous earliest-departure time over remaining energy, consume travel energy, enforce service windows, and optimize partial charging with station-specific PWL curves. PairedPiecewiseLinear Retain a dependent front over a base coordinate, compose strictly FIFO total-arrival functions, optimize waiting, enforce function-valued dependent bounds. Feasibility and two restricted cost modes are explicit. IntervalCost Choose one shared initial value in the initial interval; on every arc add its increment, enforce state/charge domains, and charge the PWL function. Minimize the full route sum over that choice. SlopeIntervalCost Retain prepared slope segments through translation, restriction and addition, with an explicit front-operation policy. SlopePaired Retain prepared slope relations with general arrival composition, waiting and function-valued bounds, explicit operation policy and absolute-final or final-minus-initial cost normalization. Runtime validation is deferred. Selection Intersect the remaining value domain with arc and vertex masks; reject an empty domain. Up to 64 values are supported. Optional vertices gives one mask per vertex. Forward extension checks the head; backward extension checks the tail. With relaxed, an unremembered vertex resets the domain to initial after checking feasibility, forgetting earlier arc and vertex eliminations. The routing master remembers all vertices of minimal violating intervals, including both endpoints. This also applies with omitted vertex masks. Incumbents always use the exact rule. SimultaneousPickupDelivery Deliver before picking up at each stop, with all route deliveries loaded at departure. Enforce capacity at departure and between all stops, admitting loads up to capacity + tolerance (default 1e-6, also used by load dominance; 0 is exact). CumulativeCost Update x += increment[arc], then add x * weight[arc] to the objective. Optional sink_upper and source_upper are the resource's upper bounds at the sink and source. With nonnegative data, dominance reads sink_upper as a bound on the weight of any completion (a forward label with a larger x pays (x_a - x_b) * sink_upper) and source_upper as a bound on the increments of any prefix (backward labels). CustomResource Zero-initialized cumulative state and cost: x += increment[arc], then charge x * weight[arc]. Optional forward_bound and backward_bound provide independent dominance constants. No vertex transition or hard state bounds. Dependent Update y += offset[arc] + factor[arc] * parent_after; reject values outside the declared closed bounds. The parent must be an earlier numeric resource. PiecewiseLinearDependent Update y += function[arc](parent_after) within the function's finite argument domain, then enforce the dependent state bounds. PiecewiseLinearResource Replace x with function[arc](x_before), enforcing the input domain and output window. PiecewiseLinearCost Add function[arc](parent_after) to the objective without changing the parent. The function domain remains a constraint in phase I. For simultaneous pickup/delivery the state is total deliveries D, net pickupsminus deliveries N, and the greatest prefix value M of N, including zero.After a service (d,p), update D += d, N += p-d, M = max(M,N) and requireD+M <= capacity. This is sufficient for the completed route: its departureload is D, and its maximum load is D+M. Increasing D at a later stop alsochecks the load required at earlier stops. Two independent delivery/pickuptotals would miss that constraint. Deliveries and pickups must be nonnegative. Cumulative weights, increments and affine dependency coefficients may be signedbut must be finite. Arithmetic overflow is reported as an error. Dependencies usethe parent's value after its transition on the same arc, and do not wait orclamp to bounds. These are explicit modeling contracts; arbitraryexternal dependency-type conventions are not asserted to have identical semantics. CustomResource exposes the fixed cumulative-style custom family separately fromCumulativeCost. It shares the numeric kernel, joins, dependency handling anddirected path certification, but always starts its state and objective at zero.Signed finite increments and weights are allowed. forward_bound promises anupper bound on the total weight of any completion; backward_bound promises anupper bound on the increments of any prefix. These optional constants only helpdominance with nonnegative increments and weights. They do not impose hardfeasibility limits, and omitting them keeps conservative dominance. Both must befinite and nonnegative when supplied. Rust uses CoupledResource::CustomResource { increments, weights, forward_bound, backward_bound }. Python usesmodel.add_custom_resource(increments, weights, forward_bound=None, backward_bound=None).For example, increments [2, 1] and weights [3, 4] charge 2*3 + 3*4 = 18.The JSON descriptor retains its own kind: {"kind":"custom_resource","increments":[2,1],"weights":[3,4],"forward_bound":7,"backward_bound":3}
 There is no initial parameter. This descriptor is a built-in numeric costresource; use CoupledPlugin for extension-defined feasibility callbacks. Piecewise-linear functions have at least two knots [argument,value], strictlyincreasing finite arguments, and finite adjacent argument/value differences.They are continuous and may increase, decrease or have flat segments. Exactknots return the supplied value. Interpolation uses (x-x0)/(x1-x0), theny0 + t*(y1-y0), clamped to the segment's endpoint value range to preservemonotonicity despite rounding. Outside-domain arguments are infeasible; noextrapolation, resource waiting or state clamping is introduced.

title: Coupled resources
heading: Explicit slope encodings for numeric resources
text:
Explicit slope encodings for numeric resources The encoded numeric variants preserve the supplied function representation:EncodedPiecewiseLinearResource, EncodedPiecewiseLinearDependent, andEncodedPiecewiseLinearCost. Existing knot-based variants and their constructorskeep their current behavior. A slope function is evaluated with ordered segmentmultiply/add operations, rather than converting it into argument/value knots.Those two evaluation methods can differ for fractional arguments. Prepared slope pairs have a distinct layout: the first pair is(value_at_lower, lower_argument); each remaining pair is(slope, segment_end). A single prepared pair is a point function. An affineinput pair instead means (intercept, slope) and must be prepared over a domain;it is not a point or a knot pair. from pybaldes import EncodedFunction, ResourceModel

function = EncodedFunction.slope_segments(
    [(2.0, 0.0), (3.0, 5.0), (-1.0, 10.0)],
    policy="strict_domain",
)
assert function.value(2.0) == 8.0
assert function.value(7.0) == 15.0
assert function.value(11.0) is None
copy = EncodedFunction.from_dict(function.to_dict())

model = ResourceModel()
resource = model.add_encoded_piecewise_linear_resource(
    initial=0.0, lower=0.0, upper=100.0,
    functions=[function],  # One function per physical arc, in insertion order.
)
 strict_domain rejects arguments outside the exact stored domain.native_tolerance explicitly selects the recovered endpoint comparison policy,which may snap arguments just inside or outside the endpoints. It does not applythat tolerance to other resources or interior knots. Both policies reportnonfinite/intermediate overflow as an error. An outside-domain result is None;a genuine function value of 1e12 remains a value. Dictionary/JSON round tripsretain the encoding and policy and validate their contents. Raw-domain image, preimage and directed-certificate proofs remain conservative.Unknown bounds retain candidates; native-tolerance preprocessing must not discardaccepted near-boundary states using the nominal endpoints. Phase I still enforcesfunction domains while suppressing objective contributions. Raw interval andpaired-front support is separate work and is not provided by the numeric variants.The implementation and tests are written, with compile checks completed; runtimevalidation of this new API is deferred at the user's request during concurrent work. SlopeIntervalCost provides a separate free-entry interval resource using preparedslope functions. The Python builder isadd_slope_interval_cost(initial_lower, initial_upper, lower, upper, increments, functions, policy="strict_domain"). Functions must be slope-encoded; knotconversion is rejected. The alternate operation policy native_front_algebrarequires functions with leaf policy native_tolerance; strict_domain requiresmatching strict leaves. This keeps function evaluation and front operationchoices explicit. Each forward extension translates the coordinate, restricts the allowed domain,adds the charge front and scans its segment endpoints for a minimum. Backwardlabels retain ordered suffix replay for the final joined objective. Unprovedoperations produce an explicit incomplete result. Unsupported dominance,completion bounds, fixing and certificates remain conservative. The result is aminimum of the computed front algebra, not a promise of a global minimum overevery sequential binary64 evaluation of the source program. Compile checks pass;new runtime regressions remain deferred.

title: Coupled resources
heading: Free-entry interval costs
text:
Free-entry interval costs IntervalCost { initial, bounds, increments, functions } retains a continuouspiecewise-linear cost function in each physical label. Unlike a deterministicbase state, its initial value is chosen over the whole route. Minimizing each arcor each half independently is invalid: charges x and -x on [0,4] jointlycost zero, although their independent minima sum to -4. Forward extension shifts the cost frontier by the arc increment and adds thecharge at the arrival state. Backward extension pulls the suffix frontier andcharge back through that increment. Joins intersect domains and minimize the sumat the common state, correcting the independently minimized prefix/suffix costs.Signed increments, signed/nonmonotone continuous charges, singleton feasibleintersections, and multiple independent interval resources are supported. Initialand global windows must be finite, nested closed intervals. Every arc has oneincrement and one charge function. Charge domains remain constraints in phase I. These fronts participate in pricing, original-cost replay, cuts, fixing,enumeration, retained repricing and node forks. CoupledLabelState::interval_cost_frontsexposes the current knots in declaration order. A frontier cannot be a numericdependency parent because it has no single arrival value. Reversal reuse remainsdisabled for this family. Production dominance normally requires equal costfronts. Domain inclusion is sufficient for the restricted all-zero front withzero future charges; frozen-front comparisons additionally require independentscalar and resource accounting. A current normalized front difference alone isnot a certificate for future rounded additions. Completion caches do notapproximate missing frontier correlations. Floating-point operations can report arithmetic failure. A translation that mergesdistinct frontier knots is rejected rather than silently dropping a cheaperinitial choice. Directed witness replay supports conservative objective intervalsfor exact integral state translations, argument knots and window endpoints withinits bounded exact domain; other cases return unknown. These intervals may beloose and do not establish an original-domain pricing certificate. This is an explicit additive-transition interval-front contract. Use the pairedrelation below for function-valued transitions with waiting. Raw externaldescriptor import and tolerance parity are separate work. from pybaldes import ResourceModel

model = ResourceModel()
model.add_interval_cost(
    initial_lower=0.0, initial_upper=4.0, lower=0.0, upper=4.0,
    increments=[0.0, 0.0],
    functions=[[(0.0, 0.0), (4.0, 4.0)],
               [(0.0, 0.0), (4.0, -4.0)]],
)
# Install on a two-arc physical graph: the joint resource charge is zero.

title: Coupled resources
heading: Paired function relations and waiting
text:
Paired function relations and waiting PairedPiecewiseLinear { initial, initial_base, arcs, mode } retains the leastattainable dependent value at every feasible base coordinate. The initialfunction describes the dependent value over the initial base window. EveryPairedResourceArc supplies total base arrival(t), departure-dependentincrement(t), head-dependent lower(x) and upper(x), and an integerwaiting slope. Arrival must be strictly increasing and satisfyarrival(t) >= t. It is the total arrival coordinate, not the consumption alone. For departure base t and a chosen head base x >= arrival(t), the least nextdependent value is max(previous(t) + increment(t) + waiting * (x - arrival(t)), lower(x))
 It must not exceed upper(x). Function domains also constrain the departureand head coordinates. Waiting choices, lower-bound clamping and disconnectedfeasible intervals are retained in the front; choosing one locally cheapestarrival would lose valid routes. Waiting provenance is retained per piece. PairedResourceMode::Feasibility adds no objective and permits function-valuedbounds. CostUnbounded permits signed increments and waiting slopes but requiresconstant dependent bounds shared across arcs; its name does not remove thosebounds or the finite base domains. CostBounded additionally requires positiveincrements, nonnegative waiting slopes, and an initial function no lower thanthe shared lower bound. Both cost modes charge the final dependent minimumminus the initial dependent minimum. An empty path costs zero. These restrictionsdo not apply to the existing signed IntervalCost contract. Forward extension builds the full relation. Backward labels retain an orderedphysical suffix program; joins apply that suffix to the actual forward relation.This preserves lower-bound clamping and waiting without assuming that they havean additive inverse. A feasibility adjoint is available internally, but backwardcost joins currently use replay and can cost more than a specialized suffixenvelope. Completion bounds remain conservative. Forward feasibility dominancerequires a front that covers the other front and stays below it; backwardfeasibility dominance compares known upper fronts by coverage and the oppositevalue order. Numerical comparisons use absolute tolerance 1e-4 or relative2.22e-10. Cost-unbounded fronts with an upper bound of at least 1e12 cancompensate a higher front through a cost penalty, provided the independentscalar and resource cost orders also hold. Reversal reuse is disabled. This is a numerical resource contract. Arithmetic ambiguity or excessivefront work produces an error; it is never converted to infeasibility or acomplete-pricing claim. Directed path certification currently returns unknownfor this family, including during phase I. Consequently proof-dependentenumeration/MIP transfer can decline the transfer and continue normal solving.No original-domain pricing certificate or raw external descriptor compatibilityis claimed. Phase I suppresses objective charges while retaining dependenttransitions and feasibility. Python exposes the same contract throughResourceModel.add_paired_piecewise_linear(initial_lower, initial_upper, initial, arrivals, increments, lowers, uppers, waiting, mode="feasibility"). Functionarguments are lists of (base, dependent) knots; each per-arc vector uses theoriginal arc order. waiting contains signed 32-bit integers. Mode strings are"feasibility", "cost_unbounded", and "cost_bounded".The complete network example isexamples/networks/paired_piecewise_linear.json.Its two required physical routes contribute paired costs 7 and 5. The separate raw SlopePaired variant uses prepared slope functions for everyfunction role. title: Coupled resources
heading: Label operations and current limits
text: Label operations and current limits Charging uses ChargingResourceArc entries in physical arc-vector order.Each entry supplies travel time/energy, a service-start window, service duration,and an optional cumulative energy-to-time curve. Curves strictly increase from[0,0] through the battery capacity. The initial energy and departure time areexplicit. Stations also constrain charging completion by closing time. The fullcontinuous front survives; backward joins replay their retained suffix on theactual forward state. Front work is bounded per extension and exhaustion returnsan error. Charging adds no cost, is not a numeric dependency parent, usesconservative equality dominance, and disables reversal reuse. Directed pathcertification declines this family, including in phase I. See theEVRP adapter for end-to-end pricing andschedule reconstruction. Selection labels carry the remaining domains. Simultaneous load labels carrycomposable delivery/net-load/peak summaries. Forward numeric labels carry actualvalues. Backward numeric labels carry affine entry conditions and a cumulativecost function; a join evaluates them at the forward label's actual values.Kernels containing piecewise dependencies instead retain shared continuationprograms for numeric constraints. A join replays that suffix from its actualforward entry values. Composition therefore adds a shared link rather thanmultiplying piecewise regions, and flat/nonmonotone functions need no inverse.Cumulative cost remains affine in its independent numeric coordinates; thesekernels cache diagonal cumulative-cost maps in linear per-arc space.State-dependent nonlinear charges are kept out of the backward baseline andreplayed at the actual forward entry state during joins. Each suffix carries anexact-sum interval, an absolute charge bound and a count; these provide an outwardroundoff allowance for the ordered charge sum without rescanning the wholesuffix to build a bound. Unknown/overflowing envelopes disable cost pruning.Affine-only kernelsretain the dense precomputed-map fast path. Shared programs have iterativerelease to avoid recursive destruction of long paths.Dependency constraints are therefore not tested at an invented backward arrivalvalue. All original scalar coordinates and cut/branch states still participate. Numeric transitions are prepared once per physical arc when resources areinstalled. Forward programs retain declaration order with resolved parent slots;backward programs cache the triangular affine map, offsets, entry conditions andcost coefficients. Label extension composes the cached map with its suffix.This trades per-arc storage (quadratic in numeric resource count) for avoidingrepeated matrix construction. Phase I rebuilds the cached cost terms with zeroweights while preserving the resource transitions and constraints. A symbolicmap overflow is recorded and reported if backward extension uses that arc;it does not prevent finite forward replay. Dependency preprocessing first checks each arc's declared entry/exit windows.It then propagates source-reachable numeric intervals forward and sink-compatibleintervals backward through the full graph. Rounded-addition preimages areexpanded before subtraction. Direct base-map preimages use bounded searches overordered binary64 arguments on each segment. They preserve flat portions,nonmonotone branches and rounding plateaus without requiring an algebraic inverse;segments already entirely inside the target range bypass the searches. Piecewise argument domains participate in bothpasses. Arcs with empty necessary domains are disabled without renumbering thephysical graph. The work limit is at most 64 paired passes; each descendingiterate is conservative, so stopping early only weakens pruning. Unknownarithmetic retains candidates. kernel.preprocessing() reports pass count,convergence and usable-arc counts; route_arc_possible reports the necessarycomplete-route filter for an arc. replay/replay_state still evaluate standalonepartial resource paths without the complete-route filter. Resource dominance now uses directional orders. A forward simultaneous state(D,N,M) can dominate another when all three coordinates are no larger; backwardfeasibility only needs D and M, so backward net load may differ. Selectedvalue domains use superset dominance. Forward dependency dominance propagatespossible comparison directions through the earlier-parent chain. A smallerstate is allowed when the lower window is protected by nonnegative increments;a larger state is allowed when nonpositive increments protect the upper window.Negative factors reverse the parent comparison. Competing effects retain bothpossible directions and must satisfy both protections, otherwise dominance isrejected. Preparation encloses every intermediate operation over declared andprepared numeric domains, and unequal comparisons require finite arithmetic.Both entry states must lie in those domains. Equality remains available whenthese sufficient conditions cannot establish an order; backward conditions keepthe existing identical-expression/window-implication rule. Piecewise slopesigns participate in forward order propagation when the prepared parent domainis contained in every arc function's domain. Backward nonlinear comparisonsrequire identical continuation programs before applying cost compensation. Aflat function still constrains its parent through the argument domain; outputequality does not erase that constraint. Unbounded cumulative parent comparisonsalso retain directional guards against overflow unique to the dominator.Direct base maps retain equality dominance until a whole-map feasibility orderis established. Parents of arbitrary nonlinear cost functions retain equality(including differences induced by ancestors), so cost-free numeric comparisonscannot discard a better future objective. Charged-resource dominance separately orders physical scalar reduced costs andaccumulated numeric costs before considering the mixed label key. Equal numericinputs retain the repaired baseline rule. Unequal inputs can use a preparedzero-compensation proof for cumulative-cost models, optionally combined withselection and simultaneous loads: nonnegative increments and weights permit0 <= a <= b; nonpositive increments and weights permit b <= a <= 0.Both cones produce ordered nonnegative future charges, and the dominator'saccumulated numeric charge must also be nonnegative. Zero-weight coordinatesretain directional overflow guards. Signed cases outside those cones retainconservative equality conditions. Dependency/domain checks remain mandatory.Composite numeric/dependency models keep the baseline identity rule because thebroader checks did not improve the measured workload. No positive current-keymargin or cost compensation is spent by charged forward dominance. Backward dominance requires identical continuation programs, compatible entrywindows and numeric state, with its outward coefficient-difference bound whereapplicable. Unknown arithmetic retains both labels; an overflow during actualextension is reported rather than silently proving route infeasibility. Completion pruning now includes an outward lower bound on the cumulative joincorrection. The engine builds direction-wide hulls of actual retained numericstates and suffix cost coefficients after labeling. Individual bucket scansuse narrower per-bucket hulls, while inherited completion minima keep thebroader hull that includes predecessor candidates. Per-bucket compatibilitychecks also use selected-domain unions, simultaneous-load envelopes andsupported backward affine entry conditions. Skipping one bucket's scan neverskips its predecessor traversal. Each completion query fixesits own state and bounds the opposite states. This works with signed coefficientswithout assuming a finite walk length. The two dot products in the implementedjoin are enclosed separately, preserving their floating-point evaluation scope.Missing hulls or arithmetic overflow leave the bound unknown and retain thecandidate. These bounds are used by pricing, completion, fixing and directionalenumeration; they are not scalar-only original-domain certificates. Hulls are rebuilt after fresh/continued labeling and discarded on new pricing,continuation or node forks. If elementarity or physical topology changes afterresource installation, reinstall the definitions so prepared dominance domainscannot become stale. Replacing the resource preparation also invalidates labelsat unchanged scalar arc costs. Forward-prefix reversal reuse is available for symmetric selection masks andsimultaneous loads with symmetric physical-arc quantities, integral deliveriesand pickups, and capacity at most 2^52. Uniform-sign net increments retain theoriginal compact reuse rule. Mixed signs additionally track an internal suffixpeak R = max suffix net load, updated by R = max(0, R + pickup - delivery).Reversing the arc sequence swaps prefix and suffix peaks; publicload_summaries() remains (D,N,M). Mixed-sign reuse builds a union of the two feasible prefix orientations. Eachload resource retains a prefix while D+M <= capacity or D+R <= capacity.With several resources this may retain extra prefixes whose feasible orientationsdiffer; every complete join still checks all resources in the actual physicalroute orientation. Dominance preserves both roles through ordered D,N,M,R.Standalone extension/replay and ordinary backward labels remain strictly feasible.Single-orientation completion hulls, completion-existence fixing and arbitraryordinary completion callbacks cannot certify this union, so those pruningoperations conservatively decline in the mixed reuse path. The scalar resource/depot symmetry checks and conservative reduced-cost potentialchecks must also pass. Numeric and PWL resources, fractional loads, asymmetricresource events and presence rows retain ordinary directional labeling.Phase-I cost suppression does not make a numeric resource reversible. Pricing,fixing and enumeration use the same eligibility rules. Arithmetic failuresinvalidate completion instead of proving that no route exists. The physical graph retains its ordinary 1024-vertex limit. There is no extra1024-state expansion limit on this production path. Labels remain subject tonormal label, time and path limits. A cyclic graph without a justified routelength/resource bound can still exhaust those limits. Integer witnesses use outward interval replay for coupled feasibility andobjective contributions. A straddling boundary or unsupported arithmetic remainsunknown. Original-domain scalar relaxation collectors and additive-costcertificates do not silently claim support for coupled resources. Generalexternal dependency-type semantics and exact native dominance/bound policiesare not claimed to match the reference binary.

Python and network JSON Build Python with maturin develop --features multi-time-windows (or add thatfeature to the existing wheel build). The stateful solver exposes: solver.set_vertex_time_windows(1, 0, [(8.0, 12.0), (16.0, 20.0)])

  "time_windows": [null, [[8, 12], [16, 20]], null],
  "bounds": [[0, 30], [0, 18], [0, 30]]
}

Exact incumbent validationalso applies union membership using its exact arithmetic. Bucket propagation projects across gaps, and component/reachability constructionincludes the image of a whole bucket cell. title: Finite column imports
heading: Finite column imports
text: Finite column imports Documentation index With clp, Rust callers can import finite column domains throughmaster::mp::imported. Routing networks are optional. Importedcolumns are original-vector patterns, so this interface also supports finitenon-routing models without constructing synthetic routes.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Model contract
text: Model contract Supply the ordinary shared Problem<D>, original MasterVariable definitionsand a list of imported::Subproblem definitions. Each subproblem declares: A nonnegative ID, distinct from other imported subproblems and routing IDs. The original variable IDs in its coordinate support. Nonnegative total multiplicity bounds, with an optional infinite upper bound. Its complete declared list of columns. Each imported::Column has a local ID, additional objective cost, nonnegativequantity bounds, an integrality flag and coalesced (original_variable_id, coefficient) entries. IDs need only be unique within their subproblem. Entriesmay be signed or fractional. An omitted entry has coefficient zero. For every original variable declared by any imported subproblem, the interfaceadds the equality x = sum(coefficient * column_quantity) over all participatingimports. Several subproblems may contribute to the same original variable.Declared supports with no columns still imply zero contribution. Originalvariables outside all imported supports remain independent master variables.Original shared rows and original-variable bounds constrain these aggregatevalues. Routing networks continue to contribute their own ordinary shared-rowcoefficients. The objective includes both original-variable costs and each column's additionalcost. To supply the whole pattern cost in Column::cost, set the correspondingoriginal-variable costs to zero. If an original variable represents a nonlinearper-pattern feature, callers supply that feature's actual coefficient in eachcolumn; this interface does not discover or separate nonlinear cuts. The declared columns define this finite domain. Importing a subset of anexternal pricing problem does not establish completeness for that largerproblem. Every declared column is loaded immediately; this is not a dynamicpricing callback.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Solving and restricting snapshots

title: Finite column imports
heading: Extending a declared domain
text: Extending a declared domain node.solve_with_columns(subproblem_id, additional_columns, options) solves anew declared model containing the old and additional columns. IDs must be newwithin that existing subproblem, and entries must use its declared originalcoordinate support. Repeated extensions are supported; duplicate IDs andinvalid definitions are errors that leave the parent usable. Explicit with_variable_bounds, with_column_bounds, with_multiplicity,with_routing_multiplicity, with_row, with_presence_row,with_registered_cut_row, with_composite_cut_row,with_resource_knapsack_row and fix_routerestrictions survive the rebuild. They are replayed by original IDs andqualified column IDs, so a changed internal allocation does not retarget a fix.with_multiplicity addresses imported groups; with_routing_multiplicityaddresses total route use in a routing subproblem. fix_route(route_index, quantity)fixes additional integer copies of a registered routing path. Rebuilds preserveits physical arc path and quantity, subtract its contribution from every sharedrow and remaining route multiplicity, and retain its objective contribution.Fixed copies still count against group multiplicity and contribute their costsand original vectors. Ordinary low-level child snapshots obtained throughnode.node() are separate objects; only the import wrapper's explicitrestrictions are replayed by this extension operation. Use node.with_row(row, routing_coefficients, original_coefficients) to add ashared restriction. Original coefficients are (original_variable_id, value)pairs; generated imported-column IDs are rejected. Routing coefficients usemp::RowCoefficients, with physical arc order and an optionalonce-per-route term. Omitted coordinates and routing families contribute zero.Coefficients must be finite and coalesced. The caller supplies a valid cut orbranch restriction. Original-coordinate links apply the row to new importedvectors automatically. Rebuilds replay the row and subtract any fixed routingcontribution, whether the row was added before or after fixing. node.with_presence_row(row, presence_coefficients, original_coefficients)couples nonlinear routing-event presence to original coordinates. It usesmp::PresenceCoefficients, with event lists aligned to physicalarcs, and supports both pair-count and any-pair semantics. The originalpresence descriptor survives extension. Fixed routes contribute their exactpresence coefficient before preprocessing the rebuilt model; imported vectorscontribute through the specified original-coordinate coefficients. The import snapshot and multi-group session also exposewith_registered_cut_row(row, routing, original),with_composite_cut_row(row, routing, original) andwith_resource_knapsack_row(row, routing, original). These accept the sameregistered cut or resource-load descriptors as ordinary routing snapshots,plus coefficients on original imported coordinates. Composite rows sum everysupplied kernel, including repeated descriptors on one routing group. Resourcerows retain the routing adapter's monotone binary-grid load and <= requirements.Their descriptors survive source batches, phase-I recovery, domain extensionand tree descendants. Original-domain certificates may remain weak for thesekernels. A correct restricted LP does not establish certified optimality; completerouting enumeration can supply the finite-domain proof after external sourcesare complete. Rebuilds install all routing kernels before replayingfixed-route contributions or running preprocessing. Callers remain responsiblefor the validity of the supplied row. Adding columns can invalidate bounds, zero fixings and infeasibility deductionsmade from the previous finite domain. The implementation therefore retains theoriginal input definition, rebuilds the model, replays explicit restrictions andreruns preprocessing and routing pricing. It starts with unknown lower boundsand discards old certificates, smoothing, cached columns and derived bounds.Even a zero-time solve of the expanded domain cannot inherit a narrower-domaincertificate. The supplied options configure this fresh solve. An empty additionresumes the unchanged snapshot and preserves its valid bounds. This operation rebuilds and reloads the declared model; it is not an incrementalpricing callback or a claim that an external pricing problem is exhausted. Theoriginal definition is retained once and shared between snapshots for thispurpose. Callers obtain values through the returned output's new identity map. node.node() exposes the ordinary immutable snapshot for preprocessing, trees,additional shared rows and MIP. Use node.values(&output.master_values) to decodevalues returned by those operations on this snapshot's descendants. Root solvesrelax declared integrality; tree or MIP enforces it. Pure imports have a completecolumn domain immediately, so solve_enumerated_mip needs no enumeration step.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Numerical pricing requests
text: Numerical pricing requests session.pricing(options) optimizes the currently known restricted master andreturns ImportPricing. It disables finite-domain preprocessing, smoothing andenumeration so deductions from the known columns cannot become assumptionsabout future columns. A pricing point carries no bound or completion flag. point.costs() exports an ImportCosts objective: additional column cost plusper_column plus the sum of each original vector entry times its coordinateprice. The constant includes base and explicit multiplicity restrictions.point.reduced_cost(column) validates a proposed new, zero-lower-bound columnand evaluates its numerical reduced cost with the same reconstructed row maps.Original-coordinate objective costs enter through these duals; do not add thema second time. These are numerical search signals, not certified lower bounds. point.reduced_cost_bounds(column) returns an enclosure of that candidate'sexact-real reduced cost at the stored binary64 dual point. Exact expansionspreserve cancellation; directed intervals handle fractional underflow. Nonemeans arithmetic could not establish a finite enclosure; invalid candidatesremain errors. An upper endpoint below zero establishes a negative reduced costfor that candidate. A nonnegative lower endpoint establishes nonnegativity forthat candidate only. Neither result covers other columns or completes anexternal domain. Phase-I requests automatically omit original objective costs. Objective pricing fixes artificial quantities to zero before accepting duals.If the objective pass did not retain necessary routing paths, recovery obtainsfeasible paths from phase I and rebuilds their identities and original costs.A small finite artificial penalty therefore cannot by itself block an otherwisefeasible restricted-domain pricing request. A pricing request requires an optimal feasible restricted master. An empty orinfeasible restricted domain may need additional feasibility columns; the APIreturns an error rather than concluding that the external domain is infeasible.Numerical pricing requests publish no external-domain bound. Separate opt-incertificate requests are described below. Use the collection protocol to accept columns;only explicit enumeration completion permits the final declared-domain solve. For a restricted domain missing feasibility columns, usesession.feasibility_pricing(options). It minimizes artificial activity withall real objective costs zero, including imported columns, original coordinates,routing arcs and fixed route costs. The returned point haskind() == ImportPricingKind::Feasibility; restricted_violation() reportsnumerical artificial activity in the current restricted master. Positiveactivity does not prove the external domain infeasible, and zero activity doesnot complete that domain. ImportCosts.kind identifies the pricing objective. In feasibility mode,ignore additional column costs and minimize only per_column plus the vectorentries times coordinate prices. reduced_cost handles this distinctionautomatically. After generating feasibility columns, request ordinary objectiveprices to continue optimization. These phase-I signals are numerical; they donot constitute an exact Farkas certificate for an unknown domain. Time-limitedor unsolved augmented masters return an error instead of a stale pricing point.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Permitted column envelopes
text: Permitted column envelopes session.with_envelope(ColumnEnvelope { cost_lower, coordinates }) declaresrestrictions on every column in that imported group, including future columns.cost_lower bounds the additional Column.cost; each (original_id, Bounds)entry bounds one vector coordinate. Declare every coordinate in the group'ssupport exactly once. Omitted column entries mean zero. Known columns mustalready satisfy the declaration. Repeated envelopes intersect, preservingprevious restrictions. Collection and direct extension reject violations, and envelopes persist throughcompletion, snapshots and later extensions. A declaration is model input; itmust describe the intended domain. It is not inferred from the known columns. point.envelope_reduced_cost_bound() encloses the minimum reduced cost over thepermitted feature box and cost floor at the stored dual point. It relaxescorrelations, so it also covers unseen permitted columns. Objective pricinguses the additional-cost floor; phase-I pricing uses zero real cost. An adverseunbounded coordinate or missing cost floor can yield negative infinity. Nonemeans no envelope was declared or arithmetic could not establish a bound. Algebraic candidate queries may evaluate symbolic vectors outside the envelope;model acceptance still enforces it. This is useful for constructing the affineobjective intercept. An envelope reduced-cost bound alone does not establish afull-master bound, external feasibility or enumeration completion.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Certificates for open domains
text: Certificates for open domains session.objective_certificate(options) requests a conservative objective lowerbound over the retained finite imports, original routing domains, and everyfuture column permitted by this open group's envelope.session.feasibility_certificate(options) instead bounds the zero-real-costfeasibility model. Its strict positivity proves infeasibility for that declaredmodel. session.infeasibility_certificate(options) returns Some only whenthat strictly positive proof is available. Otherwise it returns None. ImportCertificate exposes kind(), lower_bound() and proves_infeasible().These requests are opt-in; ordinary pricing remains numerical. They do not marka collection complete or enable a final finite-domain solve while it is open. Publication requires coverage of future columns, valid dual signs and exactfixed-route reductions. Adverse residuals at unbounded original-variableendpoints, unsupported arithmetic or an adverse missing-column price withouta finite total multiplicity cap leave the bound unknown. Declared and explicitgroup multiplicity limits both apply. A zero total cap needs no envelope; anonnegative missing-column price needs no finite cap. Corrections use the fulltotal cap, which is conservative even when known copies already consume it. Bounds inferred by projecting only the known columns are excluded from thesecertificates: future vectors can invalidate those bounds. begin_import opens one group; begin_imports below opens several together.Unselected groups retain their declared finite domains.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Several open imported groups
text: Several open imported groups node.begin_imports(&[group_ids]) creates MultiImport over one shared model.Use with_envelope(group_id, envelope) for each selected group. Unknown orduplicate IDs are rejected. Empty selections are already complete. collect and collect_priced visit unfinished groups in the requested order,round-robin, under a shared deadline and batch budget. Every pricing requestsees all accepted columns from every group. ColumnBatch.complete completesonly the requested group. pending_groups() reports the remaining groups;solve is available only after all selected domains complete. Empty nonterminalbatches consume budget and cannot starve the other groups. Errors preserve theinput session, including batches accepted earlier in the failed call. The objective/feasibility/infeasibility certificate methods cover everyunfinished group at the shared dual point. Missing coverage for any such groupkeeps publication unknown. ImportCertificate::open_groups() identifies theunfinished domains covered by that certificate. Completed groups use theiractual finite columns, even if their envelopes were coarse. Once all selectedgroups complete, finite-domain projections may be used again. An empty selectionneeds no pricing callback; use its ordinary solved output for certificates.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Automatic pricing requests during collection
text: Automatic pricing requests during collection session.collect_priced(&limits, options, callback) runs a fresh restrictedphase-I request for each batch. Positive restricted artificial activity selectsfeasibility prices; zero selects ordinary objective prices. The callbackreceives &ImportPricing and the remaining time, with all previously acceptedcolumns visible through point.subproblem(). Both LP requests share the collection deadline and respect stricter LP timelimits. A batch/time limit returns a resumable session; the next call rebuildsprices for its accepted domain. Empty nonterminal batches consume the batchbudget. Invalid data or callback errors preserve the input session, with thesame external-side-effect caveat as ordinary collection. The callback returns ColumnBatch. Its completion flag still declares fullenumeration of the intended domain. Finding no negative reduced cost does notcomplete a session or authorize a bound. This driver automates feasibility andobjective pricing requests; it supplies no global pricing certificate. As withordinary collection, synchronous callbacks must cooperate with the remainingtime argument. For mixed routing/import models, all routing families must also complete theirenumeration before the MIP can claim full-domain coverage. MIP requires highs. This interface is currently Rust-only; CLI/Python input fields are unchanged.

text:
P-step CVRP and VRPTW extension Documentation index baldes::extensions::pstep implements the compact continuous relaxation inProposition 1 of A p-step Formulation for the Capacitated Vehicle RoutingProblem, Dollevoet, Munari and Spliet. The extension is available without Cargo features. Solving requires animplementation of Baldes's LpMaster, such as Clp (--features clp). cargo build --release --features clp --bin baldes
./target/release/baldes pstep instances/cvrplib/P-n16-k8.vrp --p 2 --threads 4

 Use baldes pstep --help for time, iteration and label limits. --enumeratechecks the bound against the complete column pool; use it on small cases.The JSON separates a converged full-model lp_bound from a potentiallynonconverged restricted_objective. A work-limit error cannot certify a bound.Neither output is an integer routing solution. The fleet is unlimited even ifthe CVRPLIB instance name or header specifies a conventional truck count. Rust callers can use Problem::from_instance on a parsed inputs::Instance.It preserves the input's distance rounding. Then callProblem::solve_column_generation with an empty LpMaster andColumnGenerationOptions; pricing.p and pricing.threads control the stepsize and CPU parallelism; pricing.method selects Auto (default),Enumeration, or Bucket. The older examples/pstep.rs illustrates full-poolconstruction, and examples/pstep_cvrp.rs produces CSV benchmark records. Create a Problem with customer demands, vehicle capacity and a directed costmatrix. Matrix indices are start depot 0, customers 1..=n, end depot n+1.For a conventional single-depot instance, copy depot-to-customer costs intorow 0 and customer-to-depot costs into column n+1. None means no arc.Customer demands must be strictly positive; capacity and supplied costs mustbe finite, with nonnegative costs. The model has an unlimited homogeneous fleet. Problem::enumerate builds the complete column pool for a supplied positivep. Every partial path is elementary and capacity feasible. Paths have exactlyp arcs, except those starting at the depot, which may be shorter. Empty depotroutes are omitted. At large p, the pool contains full routes and depotprefixes; flow conservation forces incomplete prefixes to zero. The compact prior-demand choices are zero for depot starts, maximum feasibleprior demand for depot ends, and both extremes for internal paths. Coincidentextremes are stored once. A junction customer's demand belongs to both adjacentpaths; the load coefficients account for this overlap. Formulation::entries exposes sparse columns in this row order: Rows Coefficient Sense / RHS 0..n Customer degree (1 at endpoints, 2 internally) = 2 n..2n Start +1, end -1 = 0 2n..3n Start d + q_i, end -(d + q(path)) >= 0 Formulation::into_master populates an empty LP backend with nonnegativecontinuous columns. Solve through the backend's status and time-limit API.An optimal solve gives the full p-step LP bound to solver tolerance. At p=1this has the single-commodity flow bound; at p>=n+1 it has the set-partitioningbound. Bounds need not increase at every successive p; the paper guaranteesnondecrease when p is replaced by an integer multiple. The reference enumerate implementation has combinatorial cost. Both columncount and search work are bounded by EnumerationOptions. Hitting a limitreturns an error instead of returning a restricted pool as a complete model.It is intended as an exact column-pool reference for small instances and small p. price_steps solves independent jobs for each start, end and prior-demandextreme. The default Auto method uses streaming elementary enumeration whenp<=6 and the dense prefix estimate 1+n+...+n^(p-1) is at most 100,000;otherwise it uses the core bucket-graph labeling engine. This is a boundedsize heuristic, not a prediction that one backend always wins. Capacity andmissing arcs prune enumeration further. Enumeration retains just the bestpath per job, so it does not build the full column pool. Both methods solvethe same exact pricing problem and enforce work/time limits. Use --pricing enumeration or --pricing bucket to compare a specific case;--enumerate remains the independent full-pool LP cross-check. --labelslimits generated labels for bucket pricing and attempted extensions forstreaming enumeration. JSON reports these separately as generated_labelsand enumerated_extensions, and records the requested and selected methods.Exceeding either budget aborts pricing without certifying convergence. For bucket pricing, hop count is an equalityresource, preventing artificial waiting from creating extra arcs. Capacity isdisposable: every load window has lower bound zero, so waiting never helps anda cheaper label using less capacity safely dominates. Reduced costs use actualcustomer demands, not any resource waiting. Customer startsrequire exactly p arcs; depot starts allow 1..p. The fixed endpoints and extrememake the reduced cost additive along arcs, including degree, endpoint and loadduals. Each returned path is replayed against the master coefficients. Workers share immutable instance costs and duals. Each owns its searchstorage and results. Results are merged in fixed job order and all threadsjoin before the main thread updates the LP. threads=1 runs the same pricingalgorithm, making serial/parallel results reproducible. Parallel overhead mayoutweigh the benefit on very small cases. The solver starts with degree artificials, uses exact pricing to complete phaseI, and then switches to travel costs. Convergence requires every pricing jobto finish without a negative reduced-cost step at the requested tolerance.Steps are deduplicated by node order and prior demand. LP columns are added inbatches. Restricted-master objectives are not full-model lower bounds untilpricing converges. Reported bounds are numerical, not independently certified. For p<=3 the path topology itself enforces elementarity. For p=4, a relaxedbucket solve is sufficient when its minimum is elementary. Otherwise, pricingpartitions by the first arc and forbids later returns to its head. Each resultingfour-arc path is elementary; every feasible elementary step belongs to onepartition. The relaxed minimum also bounds these partitions. Longer steps useexact cycle exclusion around bucket solves: a cyclic relaxed minimum branches onforbidding each arc of a detected cycle. Every elementary path lies in at leastone child; relaxed costs bound each child. This avoids the core's 15-elementlocal NG mask limit. It can still require exponential work for larger p.PricingOptions bounds total labels and bucket subproblems per endpoint job,as well as worker count and time. Exceeding a pricing limit returns an error. Time windows, cuts, integer solving and integration with Baldes'sbranch-and-price tree are not implemented here. For integeroptimization of this compact model, impose binary aggregate arc flows, asin equations (7)–(9); making extreme p-step columns binary is not equivalent.The exposed paths and coefficients provide the data needed for a separatearc-flow integrality implementation. Run node scripts/benchmarks/benchmark_pstep.mjs ./target/release/baldes from the repositoryroot to repeat the known-instance validation and serial/parallel timing checks.It writes raw JSON and CSV records under results/pstep/ (override withPSTEP_OUT) and comparesevery bound with full column enumeration. Add --grid to run p=2,3,4 on all three bundled CVRPLIB instances, with fourworkers, 120 seconds per solve and five million labels per endpoint job. Gridrecords go under results/pstep-20261020/p234/. Reference enumeration is omittedfor the larger p=4 pools and A-n32-k5 at p=3, whose pool exceeds the CLI's columnlimit. Pricing stops are recorded explicitly, without a claimed LP bound. The validation runs gave these numerical bounds (four workers, developmentprofile).  --gpu is the CLI shorthand for --pricing cuda. PricingMethod::Cuda runs exact elementary enumeration for each endpoint/loadextreme on an NVIDIA GPU. It supports effective p <= 6, uses double precision,and preserves CPU enumeration traversal and tie order. It is opt-in; Autokeeps selecting CPU methods. The LP and reduced-cost replay remain on CPU.threads applies to CPU methods; CUDA reports zero CPU pricing workers. The prototype allocates and transfers data each round. Timing includes thesecosts, synchronization, and result replay. Runtime errors and extension limitsabort the entire round. The deadline is checked after synchronization: an activekernel is not preempted, and an over-budget result is discarded. Large p orlarge dense instances can therefore overrun a requested wall-clock limit. The synthetic benchmark warms every configuration once, then alternates fivemeasured rounds on identical problems and duals, comparing every returned path.The CVRPLIB script uses three fresh-process runs per configuration, alternatesCPU/CUDA order, fixes rounding to none, and checks converged LP bounds.

title: P-step CVRP and VRPTW extension
heading: Time windows
text:
Time windows The CLI automatically enforces finite service-start windows in Solomon inputs: cargo build --release --features clp,cuda --bin baldes
./target/release/baldes pstep instances/Solomon/C201.txt --p 3 --gpu --rounding none --json c201-gpu.json
./target/release/baldes pstep instances/Solomon/C201.txt --p 3 --pricing enumeration --threads 16 --rounding none --json c201-cpu.json

cargo run --release --features cuda --example pstep_vrptw_bench -- instances/Solomon/C201.txt instances/Solomon/C202.txt
 Rust callers use TimeWindowProblem::from_instance. TimeWindowProblem wrapsthe existing CVRP data and adds windows and service durations for both depotcopies and every customer. Travel duration equals travel cost, in the same unitsas the windows. Finite ordered windows and nonnegative service times are required.Auto uses CPU enumeration; Cuda uses the GPU; bucket pricing is currentlyunsupported for this model. CUDA still requires effective p <= 6. The master has four blocks of n rows: degree, endpoint flow, cumulative load,and service-start flow. A timed step contributes its start time positively atits first customer and its end time negatively at its last customer. Servicestarts of outgoing steps must therefore cover incoming end times. This followsthe endpoint-time extension in Vaes (2022), sections 3.2–3.3. For a fixed path, propagation represents its earliest end service time asmax(start + transit, barrier). transit includes service on each arc's tail;barrier accounts for waiting. Latest feasible starts are bounded by everyvisited due time. Pricing considers the nondominated earliest schedulingbreakpoint and the latest feasible start, together with the existing loadextremes. This retains compatible time assignments in the master instead ofonly filtering individually feasible segments. The result remains an unlimited-fleet LP relaxation, with no integer routecertificate. The JSON identifies problem: VRPTW and time_windows_enforced.A converged LP bound is distinct from a restricted-master objective. GPU/CPUcomparisons must use identical rounding; the examples explicitly use none.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: EVRP implementation status
text: EVRP implementation status Documentation index baldes::extensions::evrp is the initial model and independent schedule replay layer.It supports deterministic directed travel with separate time, energy and cost,delivery capacity, customer service-start windows, repeat charging-stationvisits, and explicit partial charging with station-specific piecewise-linearcurves. Fixed-sequence charging optimization and reference bidirectional directpricing and a two-phase subpath prototype are available. Both feed the sameroute-based LP master and column-generation adapter. Charging curves map energy to cumulative time from empty. Charging from ato b takes T(b) - T(a); charge_for applies the inverse curve and caps atfull charge. Knots must start at zero and increase strictly in both coordinates.Non-concave charging profiles are accepted. Energy and time units are suppliedconsistently by callers. Problem::replay takes an explicit closed route with an amount charged pervisit and an initial departure time. The vehicle starts full. It reports everyarrival, service start, departure and arrival/departure energy, plus totaltravel cost and delivered load. Charging follows station service and mustfinish by closing; customers only require service start within their window.Waiting is allowed and consumes no energy. A route can cover a customer subset,but cannot repeat customers or contain intermediate depots. Comparisons usestrict floating-point bounds with no implicit tolerance. Travel costs must benonnegative; pricing reduced costs are not inputs to this validator. Replay checks feasibility of a supplied charging schedule, not optimalityof its charging decisions. Tariffs, charger congestion, regeneration, mixedvehicle compatibility and station insertion are not implemented.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: Fixed stop sequence optimizer
text: Fixed stop sequence optimizer Problem::optimize_fixed_order(order, departure, ChargingOptions::default())chooses continuous partial charging amounts on a supplied sequence of customersand stations. It minimizes completion time. Travel cost is fixed by thatsequence, and charging has no separate monetary cost in the current model.Station visits may repeat; customer visits must be elementary. The algorithm propagates piecewise-affine earliest departure time as a functionof exact remaining energy. At a station, for cumulative charging time T andincoming time function F, it evaluatesT(x) + min { F(q) - T(q) : q <= x }. On each affine interval the minimum isattained at an endpoint or at q = x. All these candidates are generated;their lower envelope is split at domain endpoints and function intersections.The construction permits non-concave charging curves without an energy grid.Time-window waiting is another piecewise-affine operation. Every retained piecekeeps its predecessor and energy mapping for schedule reconstruction. The result distinguishes Optimal, Infeasible, WorkLimit, andNumericalFailure. Optimal is the optimizer's result in floating-pointarithmetic, not an interval-arithmetic certificate. Every returned schedulepasses independent strict replay. Reconstruction that fails replay reportsNumericalFailure, never Infeasible. The work budget counts generated piecesand envelope comparisons; reaching it yields no feasibility or optimality claim.The envelope implementation prioritizes a transparent reference algorithm overlarge-instance speed. Tests compare charging allocations against independent quarter-energy gridenumeration on tiny heterogeneous/non-concave instances whose optimum lies onthat grid, and check waiting, repeated stations, exact windows and work limits.These tests do not establish performance on published benchmarks.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: Direct bidirectional pricing
text: Direct bidirectional pricing Problem::price_direct(duals, fleet_dual, departure, DirectOptions::default())prices elementary customer routes with repeatable station visits. The dualvector has one entry per location and must be zero at stations and depots.Reduced cost is travel cost minus customer duals minus one fleet dual. The bestreplay-validated route is returned even when its reduced cost is nonnegative.No subset-row cuts, ng relaxation or branching restrictions are accepted yet. The implementation uses forward earliest-departure functions F(e) andbackward latest-departure functions B(e) at exact departure energy e. Backwardfunctions exclude processing at the meeting node, already processed by theforward label. Internally backward times are negated to share lower-envelopecode. Backward extension undoes charging, station closing, service, customerwindows and travel in the appropriate order. At a station the core operationis max { B(y) - T(y) : y >= q } + T(q) - service, with station closing appliedto departure before charging is undone. Dominance conservatively requires equal visited-customer sets, no greaterreduced cost, no more used arcs and pointwise time dominance over the entireother function's domain. The function comparison covers domain gaps andinterior crossings; endpoint-only scalar tests are insufficient. Joins requirecompatible customer sets, capacity, total arc count and some common energywith F(e) <= B(e). Both directions retain energy mappings for reconstruction;every returned complete route passes strict schedule replay. This is an E1-inspired reference implementation of the coherent functionextension/dominance/join approach described byNafstad, Desaulniers and Stålhane (2025), Sections 3–4.The prefix/suffix affine-envelope construction is specific to Baldes's model;the paper's faster PWL algorithm, midpoint-by-time stopping, unreachable-customersets and acceleration techniques are not reproduced here. The current objectiveis travel cost, not the paper's separate route-duration extension. Pricing statuses are explicit: Bounded: all customer-serving routes with at most max_arcs travel arcswere covered. This does not certify that longer routes have no negative cost. Complete: that bound covers every relevant route, using customerelementarity when there are no stations, or a conservative depot-horizonbound when all available non-self travel times are strictly positive. WorkLimit / NumericalFailure: no pricing completeness claim. Any returnedincumbent remains independently replay-validated. Complete describes exhaustive model coverage in f64 arithmetic, not a rigorousreal-number reduced-cost certificate. No station-repeat bound is inferred fromzero-time travel. Nonnegative-cost self loops are omitted because they cannotimprove a schedule or customer coverage. Work/label limits and arc limits areconfigurable. Both directions currently grow to half the arc bound and comparecompatible label pairs; this prioritizes correctness evidence on tiny casesover large-instance speed. Tests compare minimum reduced costs to exhaustive stop-order enumeration withthe fixed-order optimizer, with dominance enabled and disabled. They also checkcapacity, customer elementarity, zero-time travel, work limits, bounded versusglobal coverage, and domain-interior dominance failures.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: Two-phase subpath prototype
text: Two-phase subpath prototype Problem::price_subpaths(duals, fleet_dual, departure, SubpathOptions::default())uses the same objective, dual convention, route arc limit and completenessstatuses as direct pricing. Phase one generates elementary customer ordersbetween depot/station endpoints with no interior charging. It retains all suchorders fitting a full battery and load capacity, including direct charger-to-charger moves with no customers. max_subpaths caps this phase explicitly. Phase two composes these subpaths into complete routes. It propagates theentire continuous time/energy function through every constituent customer andendpoint, optimizes charging, and checks customer elementarity and capacity.It may prune a prefix only with equal customer history, no greater reduced cost,no more arcs and full function-domain dominance. Subpaths are never suppliedas master columns. Both backends return the same complete-route representationwith a replay-validated charging schedule. The decomposition is inspired byJacquillat and Lo, v3 (2026).The prototype deliberately retains distinct phase-one orders and carries fullcharging functions in phase two. It does not implement the paper's compressedresource vectors, two-sided subpath domination, adaptive ng relaxation or cuts.Thus it does not assume that scalar forward domination can replace the paper'sdomination requirements. Keeping the full prefix state makes composition anexplicit dynamic program under this static model; the paper's speedups havenot been reproduced. Tests compare both backends with exhaustive route-order evaluation, under thesame data, duals and arc bounds, with dominance enabled and disabled. Fixturesinclude heterogeneous/non-concave charging, repeated stations, and a route withtwo consecutive charging stops in both directions. Global versus boundedcoverage and phase-one/phase-two work limits have separate checks.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: Native physical-graph backend
text: Native physical-graph backend Problem::price_native(duals, fleet_dual, departure, NativeOptions::default())uses the ordinary Baldes labeling engine. SelectEvPricingBackend::Native(NativeOptions::default()) in the shared EV master touse it in both feasibility and travel-cost phases. The reference direct andsubpath backends remain available; the default backend is unchanged. Problem::native_graph(...) also exposes the compiled Graph<3> for a nativepricing::Solver<3>. The graph preserves location IDs and duplicates the depotat vertex locations.len() as the sink. Its active scalar resources track arccount and delivered load. Only customers receive elementarity sets, so stationvisits may repeat. A native PWL boolean state records whether a customer hasbeen served; the sink requires that state to be one. Customer duals are chargedon incoming arcs and the fleet dual is charged once on source departure.The delivery-only native simultaneous-load resource additionally guards loadfeasibility and dominance without scalar epsilon comparisons. The native CoupledResource::Charging retains earliest departure time as acontinuous function of exact remaining energy. Travel consumes energy; servicestarts inside its window. Stations apply the full partial-charging envelopeT(x) + min_{q<=x}(F(q)-T(q)) and require service/charging to finish by closing.Heterogeneous and non-concave strictly increasing curves are supported withoutan energy grid. Forward labels retain owned front pieces. Backward labels retainthe physical suffix; joins replay that suffix on the actual forward front.Dominance conservatively requires equal charging fronts, and reversal reuse isdisabled. This resource adds no objective and cannot be a numeric parent. After native pricing chooses a stop order, the existing fixed-order optimizerreconstructs its charging amounts and independently replays the schedule. Afailed reconstruction reports numerical failure, never infeasibility or completepricing. max_front_work bounds each individual frontier extension, includingsuffix replay; it is not a total pricing-work budget. max_reconstruction_workseparately bounds witness reconstruction. Label limits and max_arcs bound thenative search. Resource arithmetic/state failures remain unknown; the nativeengine may aggregate a nonzero frontier-budget exhaustion into numerical failure.The work statistic counts witness reconstruction work, not native front work. This adapter currently supports at most fifteen customers, reflecting nativeexact NG local memory, and at most 1023 input locations because it adds a sink.It uses native numerical resource/cost comparisons. Complete and Boundedretain their numerical coverage meanings; no directed-rounding certificate isprovided for charging. The largest absolute reduced arc cost times max_arcsmust be below 1e12 - 1, because the native engine reserves 1e12 as a sentinel;unsupported scales are rejected explicitly and require rescaling cost units.Native cuts and restrictions can be attached to theexposed graph/solver; the shared EV master does not add cut separation or treesearch. The tiny regression comparisons establish agreement on the testedfixtures, with no performance or large-instance scaling claim.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: Supported scope and remaining extensions
text: Supported scope and remaining extensions The raw ElectricRouting.jl multi-depot data is downloaded underinstances/evrp/electricrouting-jl/:161 instances and 312 upstream reference solutions, pinned to commit102c9c90f6021d2dea664f0d8ad6990661c7668a with per-file hashes. Their nonlinear charging curves must bespecified separately to match an upstream nonlinear experiment. This implements the initial static, single-vehicle-type travel-cost EV LPworkflow. It is not an integer branch-and-price solver. Cuts, branching/ngstate, mixed fleets, tariffs, congestion, time-dependent travel, externalbenchmark parsers and large-instance performance engineering remain extensions.The E1 reference backend and E2-inspired prototype do not reproduce everyacceleration from either paper. title: Robust vehicle routing
heading: Robust vehicle routing
text: Robust vehicle routing The production robust VRPTW implementation uses the ordinary bucket graphlabeling engine and standard root/tree solvers. Labels carry budgeted demandand travel-time states in addition to their nominal bucket resources. Forwardand backward extension, dominance, and concatenation use those robust states.

title: BALDES IPM in Rust
heading: Source mapping and implementation
text: Source mapping and implementation C++ source Rust module Behavior ip_solver.h, src/ipm/ip_solver.cpp model.rs, solver/ Standard form, homogeneous self-dual Mehrotra loop, upper-bound elimination, adaptive regularization, predictor/corrector and centrality corrections, recovery hipo_ldlt.h factor/mod.rs, sparse_solver.rs::HiPOLDLT Block ordering, symbolic fill, fundamental supernodes, elimination forest, frontal assembly, child Schur updates, restricted 1x1/2x2 Bunch–Kaufman pivots, sign-preserving small-pivot regularization, refinement normal_eq_ldlt.h sparse_solver.rs::NormalEqLDLT SPD normal equations A D⁻¹ Aᵀ + Rd, followed by primal recovery sparse_solver.h sparse_solver.rs::SparseSolver Backend dispatch and structural fill estimate Eigen sparse/dense plumbing matrix.rs, factor/mod.rs Owned sparse CSC input and factors stored as sparse columns; dense arrays only for individual fronts and Schur updates The augmented matrix is [-(theta + Rp), Aᵀ; A, Rd]. The ordering preservesthe primal/dual boundary, and fundamental supernodes cannot cross it. Frontsare processed in increasing elimination order, a valid child-before-parentorder, and child Schur buffers are released after parent assembly. Child updatesstore only the lower triangle, packed by row; parents assemble that trianglewithout copying an unused upper half.Sparse augmented factors may use an up-looking row-update path when theprimal block has at least twice as many variables as rows and symbolic L hasat most 32 off-diagonal entries per system variable on average. This pathexpects negative primal and positive dual pivots; small, non-finite or wronglysigned pivots retry the existing pivoted multifrontal factorization. OriginalKKT refinement remains enabled. Sparse factor columns use contiguous CSC valuesand share an immutable pattern across numerical refactors and clones. Numeric pivot swaps are composed with the symbolic permutation and applied torows of previously assembled factor columns. Iterative refinement uses|b - Kx| / (|b| + |K||x|) with at most two correction solves. Deliberate differences from C++: Ordering keeps the independent diagonal primal block in natural order.Eliminating these vertices cannot connect other primal vertices, so buildinga primal column-intersection graph cannot reduce fill. The dual Schur graphuses deterministic exact minimum degree with explicit graph updates,rather than the shared C++ approximate minimum degree quotient graph.Complete remaining graphs are emitted directly; dense intersection graphsuse packed adjacency (at most 32 MiB), while sparse or larger graphs retaintree sets. Those graph representations produce the same ordering. Primalreordering preserves structural fill but can change floating-point sums. The normal-equations path uses this crate's multifrontal factorization,rather than the external C++ supernodal implementation. Its fixed CSC patternand row-to-column source positions are cached; refactors accumulate valuesdirectly without duplicate triplets or repeated sorting. The comparison backends LDLT, SUPERNOODAL, and FRONTAL from the siblinglinear_system directory are not separately ported or aliased to HiPO. Fixed variables are eliminated. Free variables, upper-only bounds, shiftedbounds, zero columns, mixed senses, objective offsets and row dual signsare tracked explicitly through recovery. Complementarity includes the upper-bound slack/multiplier product. Successchecks primal feasibility as well as dual feasibility and gap. Centrality corrections are added to the current Newton direction insteadof overwriting it. The homogeneous Schur denominator uses its equivalentpositive quadratic form to avoid subtractive cancellation. A singular 2x2 pivot returns a numerical error instead of replacing onlyits determinant, which would be inconsistent with the stored D block. Ruiz equilibration is implemented and enabled by default (five passes).The C++ header declares scaling routines, but its optimization loop doesnot invoke them. Set scaling_iterations: 0 to disable scaling. The internal objective is normalized after equilibration. Dual recovery anddual/gap checks undo objective scaling, retaining tolerances in originalunits. Wide upper bounds start with feasible slacks and unit complementarityproducts, avoiding a large artificial residual from bounds such as 1e12. A regularized least-squares starting estimate reduces initial row and dualresiduals before positive shifts for the HSD variables. Finite upper boundsretain unit complementarity. Unsafe estimates, empty systems and very tightbounds retain the unit initializer. This adds one factorization and two solvesper eligible LP; it is not a warm start from the previous CG solve. The restricted master selects this solver with --master ipm; the API is alsousable independently. Performance parity with theC++ solver and large-instance robustness have not been established; there isno parallel factorization, relaxed supernode amalgamation or nested dissection.

title: IPM factorization: cached assembly and lower-triangle updates
heading: Changes
text: Changes Compute CSC-to-front scatter positions and child-to-parent row maps duringsymbolic analysis. Share immutable maps across solver clones. Retain dense scratch, pivot permutations, multiplier vectors, and outputcolumn capacity across Newton steps. Reset scratch when the symbolic planchanges; solver clones start with independent empty scratch. Update the contiguous lower triangle and read symmetric pivot candidates fromthat triangle. Avoid mirroring the trailing matrix after every pivot. Theprevious full-matrix kernel remains an independent test oracle. Batch tree work over retained scratch buffers. Nested node work uses the samebounded Rayon pool; no workspace lock is held during nested execution. Recycle consumed Schur buffers through a size-binned pool, capped at 8 MiB persolver. The limit covers spare buffers, not live contributions or factors.Releasing consumed contributions avoids retaining every clique on deep trees. Preserve the serial up-looking fast path and release its old compressedfactor before allocating the next output. The dense update is still a rank-1/rank-2 kernel. title: DeLuxing column fixing
heading: DeLuxing column fixing
text: DeLuxing column fixing BALDES provides an opt-in Rust implementation of deep Lagrangian underestimatefixing, following the algorithm in RouteOpt's packages/deluxing reference.It filters a complete enumerated integer column pool before a MIP solve.Do not use these fixes to certify an incomplete restricted master: laterpricing could introduce columns that invalidate the bounds. The procedure first solves the full LP and fixes columns by reduced cost.It divides surviving columns at half the incumbent gap, clusters the vectorsrhs - column, and solves auxiliary LPs over the low reduced-cost columns.Each cluster supplies a new RHS; successful fixing rounds supply subsequentRHS vectors. Small pools use deterministic Lloyd clustering; larger pools usenorm quantiles. Seeds and deletion trajectories can differ from RouteOpt. The Rust implementation accounts for row senses, finite upper bounds, integermultiplicities and objective offsets. It projects row multipliers onto theirvalid sign cone and corrects negative reduced costs using column bounds. Animproving integer solution can use at most one column above the half-gapthreshold, which supplies the stronger bound in the auxiliary rounds. Fixingrequires a bound strictly greater than the cutoff plus a safety tolerance.
